WITH filtered_scans AS (
  SELECT 
    s.zoneref,
    s.gbsize,
    s.spanmin,
    st.healtheval
  FROM scans s
  JOIN sites st ON s.zoneref = st.zoneregistry
  WHERE s.chronotag >= '2024-06-06 11:53:59.684274'
    AND s.chronotag <= '2024-11-03 19:51:13.516797'
),
group_stats AS (
  SELECT 
    zoneref,
    healtheval,
    AVG(gbsize::float / spanmin::float) FILTER (WHERE gbsize IS NOT NULL AND spanmin IS NOT NULL AND spanmin > 0) as avg_ratio,
    COUNT(*) as scan_count
  FROM filtered_scans
  GROUP BY zoneref, healtheval
),
mean_calc AS (
  SELECT AVG(avg_ratio) as overall_mean
  FROM group_stats
  WHERE avg_ratio IS NOT NULL
)
SELECT 
  gs.zoneref,
  gs.healtheval,
  gs.avg_ratio,
  gs.scan_count,
  (gs.avg_ratio - mc.overall_mean) as beats_mean
FROM group_stats gs
CROSS JOIN mean_calc mc
WHERE gs.avg_ratio > mc.overall_mean
  AND mc.overall_mean IS NOT NULL
ORDER BY 
  beats_mean DESC NULLS LAST
LIMIT 10;

assumptions.assumption: chronotag is stored in a text format where >= and <= string comparison correctly orders chronologically (e.g., ISO 8601 timestamps)
The phrase 'between' includes both date boundaries (>= on lower, <= on upper)

alternatives.interpretation: If 'between' should be interpreted as a half-open interval [start, end), use < instead of <= for the upper bound
